dedupe_keys.name: vienna 4g 5g drive test dataset tu wien

description: The Vienna 4G/5G drive-test dataset is a city-scale open collection of georeferenced LTE and 5G New Radio measurements taken in Vienna, Austria, by researchers at TU Wien. It combines two views of the same networks: passive scanner observations, which record signals from all cells an instrument can hear, and active handset logs, which record what a user device experiences while connected. The measurements come with deployment descriptors for the serving base stations, including estimated locations, antenna azimuths and heights, and with building and terrain models of the city, so that the data can be used to train and test radio propagation and coverage models. The authors organised it for machine learning work on network analysis, planning and optimisation. It was posted as an arXiv preprint in March 2026, revised in September 2026, and published in Scientific Data. Coverage: the city of Vienna, one measurement campaign. Format and access: data files from the repository named in the Scientific Data article, free under CC BY 4.0; about 19 MB in version 2. Caveats: one city and one period; base station parameters are estimates, not operator records. Simulation uses: calibration and validation of coverage and propagation models, digital twins of urban mobile networks and resilience studies that need measured signal levels. Related records: OpenCelliD and the national antenna registers give site locations without measured signals.
